bVisor README: 'bVisor is an early proof-of-concept and should not yet be used in production.' TypeScript SDK only (npm 'bvisor'); Python SDK and CLI 'planned'. Isolation is seccomp-user-notifier syscall interception in-process (gVisor-inspired), not a VM or container; resource limits (cgroups) 'not started'. Last repo commit 2026-02-23 (about 7 months without activity).

snapshot_auto.note: Local in-process library, no hosted machines. The whole Sandbox class exposes only constructor, setLogLevel and runCmd; no snapshot/persist/restore of any kind. Sandbox state is an in-process COW overlay that lives with the host process.

snapshot_on_demand.note: SDK surface (v0.0.6) is only new Sandbox(), setLogLevel(), runCmd(); no checkpoint/fork API.

harness_api.quote: bVisor is an SDK and runtime for safely executing bash commands locally, without the need for remote sandboxes or local VMs/containers.
harness_api.note: Only a generic runCmd (bash) with stdout/stderr streams; no agent-harness integration.

ingress_rules.note: Listed under 'Blocked' syscalls: guests cannot listen at all, so there are no exposed ports and nothing to control (local library, no URLs).

guest_firewall.note: Guests run as the unprivileged host user under a seccomp user-notifier supervisor (no own kernel, no CAP_NET_ADMIN; unshare/setns/bpf blocked; setsockopt unhandled -> ENOSYS). iptables/nftables cannot work.

volume_attach.quote: bVisor is imageless, meaning it does not require a base image to run. It runs with direct visibility to the host filesystem.
volume_attach.note: No volumes: the sandbox sees the host filesystem through a copy-on-write overlay.

volume_shared.quote: Isolation is achieved via a copy-on-write overlay on top of the host filesystem. Files opened with write flags are copied to a sandbox-local directory. Read-only files are passed through to the real filesystem.
volume_shared.note: All sandboxes on a host read the same host filesystem (read-only passthrough), but writes are private per sandbox; no first-party shared volume.

isolation.quote: Inspired by gVisor, bVisor runs programs directly on the host machine, providing isolation by intercepting and virtualizing Linux syscalls from userspace.
isolation.note: Not actually gVisor and not a VM/container: bVisor is a local in-process seccomp-user-notifier syscall interceptor embedded in the calling application, running on the host's own kernel with a COW filesystem overlay. Closest listed category by mechanism (userspace syscall virtualization) but there is no separate customer machine at all -- isolation is process-level within one host, not multi-tenant machine isolation. derived.

image_oci.quote: bVisor is imageless, meaning it does not require a base image to run. It runs with direct visibility to the host filesystem.

docker_inside.quote: bVisor is an SDK and runtime for safely executing bash commands locally, without the need for remote sandboxes or local VMs/containers.
docker_inside.note: mount/unshare/setns/bpf/chroot/pivot_root syscalls are explicitly blocked (privilege escalation category), so a Docker daemon cannot run inside a bVisor sandbox.

nested_virt.note: No KVM/VM support; sandboxes run as plain unprivileged host processes via seccomp interception, not machines with /dev/kvm.

desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a local bash-execution library, not a machine with a GUI)

snapshot.note: SDK surface is only constructor, setLogLevel, runCmd; no snapshot/checkpoint/restore API of any kind.

fork.note: No clone/fork API in the SDK.

fork_running.note: No fork capability exists at all, so a running-clone variant is also absent.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork mechanism exists, so memory-preserving forks are unavailable.

pause_resume.note: No pause/resume method exists; a sandbox is just a live in-process object for the life of the host process.

wake_on_request.quote: bVisor is an SDK and runtime for safely executing bash commands locally, without the need for remote sandboxes or local VMs/containers.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (there is no hosted machine to sleep/wake -- it runs inline in the calling app)

persistent_disk.quote: Isolation is achieved via a copy-on-write overlay on top of the host filesystem. Files opened with write flags are copied to a sandbox-local directory.
persistent_disk.note: Sandbox-local writes live in a COW overlay tied to the host process; there is no documented persistence mechanism across sandbox instances/restarts.

auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no billed hosted machine that idles; lifecycle is tied to the embedding process)

lang_python.quote: [Running Python](src/sdks/node/examples/python-hello.ts) - Write and execute a Python script
lang_python.note: bVisor is imageless and passes through to the host filesystem/binaries, so any Python present on the host works inside a sandbox, as shown by the shipped example.

lang_node.quote: The bVisor runtime ships wrapped in a Typescript SDK, installed via npm.
lang_node.note: Primary SDK is a TypeScript/Node package (npm install bvisor); Node is the native runtime.

public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Server-socket syscalls (bind/listen/accept) are explicitly blocked, so sandboxes cannot expose any listening service, let alone get a public IPv4.

egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no HTTP-method/path-level egress control is documented.

secret_proxy.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no credential-injection proxy is documented.

static_egress_ip.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; there is no provider-hosted egress path to make static, since the sandbox shares the host's own network egress.

max_session_h.quote: bVisor runs programs directly on the host machine, providing isolation by intercepting and virtualizing Linux syscalls from userspace.
max_session_h.note: No hosted session to time-limit: a sandbox is an in-process object that lives as long as the embedding application process runs, with no provider-side stop policy documented. derived.

egress_allowlist.quote: Networking | socket, socketpair, connect, shutdown, sendto, recvfrom, sendmsg, recvmsg
egress_allowlist.note: Outbound connect/send syscalls are virtualized/passed through with no documented allow/deny-list controls.

root.quote: bVisor is imageless, meaning it does not require a base image to run. It runs with direct visibility to the host filesystem. ... | Identity (write) | `setuid`, `setgid`, `setreuid`, `setregid`, `setresuid`, `getresuid`, `setresgid`, `getresgid`, `setfsuid`, `setfsgid`, `getgroups`, `setgroups`, `setpriority`, `getpriority` |
root.note: bVisor runs commands as the unprivileged host user; identity-changing syscalls (setuid/setgid/etc.) are unhandled, and privilege-escalation syscalls (ptrace, mount, chroot, pivot_root, unshare, seccomp, bpf) are explicitly blocked. There is no root/sudo inside the sandbox.

custom_image.quote: bVisor is imageless, meaning it does not require a base image to run. It runs with direct visibility to the host filesystem. This allows system dependencies such as `npm` to work out of the box.
custom_image.note: The product is explicitly imageless (runs in-process on the host filesystem via a COW overlay); there is no concept of starting from a custom Docker/OCI image at all.

inbound_https.note: Listed under 'Blocked' syscalls: guest code cannot bind/listen/accept at all, so no server (HTTP or otherwise) can ever run inside a sandbox, let alone be exposed via a URL. bVisor is a local in-process bash-execution library, not a hosted machine with ports/URLs.

usage_api.quote: bVisor is an SDK and runtime for safely executing bash commands locally, without the need for remote sandboxes or local VMs/containers. The bVisor runtime ships wrapped in a Typescript SDK, installed via npm.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; Butter is a local in-process library (not a hosted service). The SDK exposes only constructor, setLogLevel(), and runCmd(). No usage API, no hosted machines to bill, no usage metrics API.
